1.why: All ten screens use a static, simple card layout with no moving images or pop-ups, though the persistent Logs panel adds extra content to every page.

2.why: Primary actions are bold blue buttons under clear headings with a highlighted security notice, though in step 8 the accept checkbox is oddly separated from its wrapped label text.

3.why: Each screen presents a single task with one labeled input and one primary button, though the required reset code must be located inside the monospace Logs panel list.

4.why: The flow forces the user through many sequential steps (email, 43-character reset token, second MFA code, new password with four composition rules, sign-in, acceptance), even though the password rules are printed on-screen.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, password-manager option, or autofill affordance is visible on any screen, including the sign-in page.

6.why: Nothing is saved or pre-filled for the user (the sign-in email field is empty and codes must be copied from logs); only the repeated layout offers some familiarity.

7.why: Instructions are short plain sentences (e.g., 'Enter your account email address'), with only mild jargon such as 'simulated trusted channel' and the technical Logs text.

8.why: No error or validation message appears in any of the ten screenshots, so there is no evidence that errors describe the problem and how to fix it.

9.why: No concrete examples of what to type are shown (no sample email placeholder, no example compliant password); only brief instructions are given.

10.why: There are no authentication-method choices: password and two codes are mandatory and no face/biometric login exists anywhere, though the link-vs-manual-code option is labeled clearly.

11.why: Every screen offers at most one primary button plus one secondary link, so the user is never confronted with many simultaneous choices.

12.why: Explicit outcome screens exist ('Password updated', 'Privacy conditions accepted', 'A second verification code was sent'), though sign-out silently returns to the start page with no explicit signed-out confirmation.

13.why: Each new step carries a one-line tip explaining what to do next, and a persistent 'Keep your account safe' tip box appears on every screen.

14.why: 'Request another code', 'Forgot password?' and 'Return to sign in' links provide retry paths, but no actual mistake-and-retry scenario (e.g., wrong code handling) is shown.

15.why: All ten steps share the identical header, card layout, button styling, security notice, and Logs panel, making the design highly consistent.
